2nov1870.summary: Steenackers, director general of telegraphs and posts at Tours, tells three colleagues in besieged Paris what line to take towards the post office: the services rendered, balloon and pigeon post, the pigeon service about to be opened to private messages, the decree uniting posts and telegraphs and the one ending the post's monopoly on carrying newspapers. He passes on a report of Prussians leaving Saint-Germain daily with pickaxes, advice on coating cotton balloons, and family news for each addressee.
2nov1870.en:
Tours, 2 November (inspectors' cipher). Steenackers to Messrs P...et, Mercadier, Le-...-e.

My dear friends. I want to [..] the attitude that seems to me required by the one taken in the rue Jean-Jacques Rousseau
[the Paris post office]: to be able to stress on every occasion the services rendered by us in Paris and at Tours; that it is above all
to the organisation set up by us here and in Paris that the capital owes not being completely cut off from the provinces;
that we have set up on a large scale communication by balloon and pigeons; that the pigeon service, at first restricted to
official [dispatches], is going to be extended to private ones; that we have quickened here the postal service, made more
difficult and slower by the disorganisation of the railways due to the war and its necessities.
